title: Release Rhythm Playbook: hosted-api release cadence & model lineup gates (quarter plan)
creator: Maya Chen
project: Hosted API + Model Catalog Quarterly Runbook
description: Create a single-source quarterly playbook that defines release cadence, canary windows, gating criteria, and rollback policies for Hosted API model lineup updates. This ticket synthesizes inputs from product, engineering, and design to lock a repeatable schedule and responsibilities for Q2 planning and execution. The playbook will be used by the release coordinator to publish a calendar, automate gating checks, and inform Dedicated/Private rollout guides.
acceptance_criteria: Published Playbook doc in Confluence with calendar and owner matrix
Gating criteria enumerated (quality, latency, cost thresholds) and mapped to automated checks
Canary windows and rollback triggers defined for hosted and dedicated environments
Cross-functional review completed by Eng, Design, Security, and Support
Onboarding checklist for model owners and SRE runbook links embedded
checklist: Draft initial cadence proposal (weekly canaries vs biweekly)
Align SLO thresholds with Reliability PM
Define model-level gating thresholds (eval pass rate >= 92%, latency + p95 <= 120ms for base tier)
Create calendar artifact and Slack reminder automation
Circulate for review and incorporate feedback
Publish final playbook and notify stakeholders
notes: Context: multiple prior artifacts exist about hosted model catalog rotations; this ticket consolidates a runnable cadence rather than strategic goals.

Trade-offs discussed: faster cadence increases ability to iterate but raises flakiness risks for downstream customers; recommended mitigations include longer canaries for high-impact models and automatic fallback to previous model family.
Decision shorthand: adopt a hybrid cadence — weekly fast lane for minor patch releases (non-breaking tokenization/quant changes), 3-week lane for model family upgrades with full eval regression runs.

Model gating will include: unit tests (smoke), eval suite (customer-facing prompts), perf gate (latency/cost), infra compatibility (runtime kernels), and security checklist (KMS integration verified for private deployments).
Metric thresholds: eval regression delta <= 1.5% relative to control, embedding cosine stability > 0.97 for canonical queries, per-request cost delta < 8% (unless explicitly approved).
Fallback policy: automatic downgrade to pinned stable model within 10 minutes if error rate > 3% for 5 minute window or p95 latency spikes > 2x baseline for 10 minutes.
Stakeholder owners: Product (release cadence), Eng (automation and checks), SRE (canary monitoring), DX (release notes & SDK compatibility), Support (customer comms).
Out-of-scope: internal Dedicated contract negotiation cadence (handled in separate PM ticket) and private on-prem upgrade automation for air-gapped sites.
